assessmentSummary.identity: A dynamic bilateral quadruped wrist-extension rocker. Start on hands and knees with palms flat, fingers spread and facing forward, elbows extended but not forced, and a firm stable hand surface. Shift the shoulders forward under control to a comfortable wrist-extension/load endpoint while maintaining the declared contacts, then rock back to the starting load. One complete forward-and-back cycle is one repetition. Forward range, tempo, brief comfortable endpoint pause, repetitions, sets, rest, and optional knee cushioning are delivery annotations. Palms up or backs of hands down, fingers turned toward the knees or sides, unilateral loading, circles, palm lifts, sustained isometric holds, tall-plank loading, raised hands, bands, manual force, or a clinical assessment changes the task.
currentCardFindings: Source 30 has one skeletal baseline variant and a generic legacy profile with empty taxonomy, anatomy, load, fatigue, constraints, support, research, alternate, calibration, and exact media review data.

The legacy exercise and USA Gymnastics/Prehab instructions consistently support one forward-facing palms-down quadruped forward-and-back rocker; Source 31 palms-up, Source 256 hold-or-tall-plank capacity, Source 32 palm lifts, and Source 796 orientation shifts remain distinct.
Legacy age, publication, link, and reviewed-media implications are unsupported and must be cleared or quarantined.
assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Select only when exact palms-down/fingers-forward floor support, comfortable wrist-extension range, elbow/shoulder support, firm surface, dose, duration, symptoms, and downstream hand-support budgets fit. Do not turn the hands, add a hold, move to tall plank, elevate the hands, or treat the drill as clearance. Choose a separately authored palms-up, isometric/tall-plank, palm-lift, orientation-shift, or raised-support card when that changed task is intended.

claims: USA Gymnastics distinguishes palms-on-floor forward rocking for wrist extension from backs-of-hands rocking for wrist flexion.
Source 30 therefore remains one palms-down, fingers-forward, dynamic forward-and-back quadruped identity; hand surface and action are not silent annotations.
The task combines a braced quadruped base with controlled upper-extremity pushing support and a sagittal weight shift.
Use controlled brace and push patterns; mobility and preparation are contextual purposes rather than invented movement-pattern keys.
Wrist extension angle and flexion moment vary with gymnastics hand-support conditions, demonstrating that support details matter.
The study examines back handsprings, not this rocker, so the card records observable position, contacts, range, exposure time, and symptoms without importing force values.
USA Gymnastics provides a hold-based example and advises fewer repetitions when form fails; it does not validate the Vortex dynamic dose.
Use a conservative review-only range of one to two sets and five to ten complete cycles, calculate actual support time, and stop before contact, range, support, or symptom quality degrades.
Prehab supports hands and knees, fingers forward, strong upper-body support, a slow shoulder-over-wrist shift, and a backward return.
The card adds exact palms-down contact, complete-cycle counting, comfortable range, no bounce, firm surface, symptom stops, and actual-dose recording.
The systematic review supports taking gymnastics wrist symptoms and accumulated exposure seriously while emphasizing low certainty and absent training thresholds.

Coach support verifies task identity, floor entry, palm/finger contact, wrist range, elbow/shoulder/trunk support, first fault, actual exposure, symptoms, downstream hand-support demand, and escalation without diagnosis.
USA Gymnastics separately lists palms-on-floor forward rocking and backs-of-hands backward rocking, supporting distinct wrist-extension and wrist-flexion tasks.

Keep palms-up, rear-facing, side-facing, circular, unilateral, palm-lift, isometric, tall-plank, raised-support, banded, manual, and assessment tasks outside the exact Source 30 variant until separately authored and reviewed.

alternateAssessments.name: Wrist Rockers, Wrist Rocks, or Quadruped Wrist Extension Rocks
alternateAssessments.rationale: These aliases fit only when the exact bilateral palms-down, fingers-forward, quadruped forward-and-back cycle is stated.

alternateAssessments.name: Smaller Forward Range
alternateAssessments.rationale: Comfortable forward range changes dose while contacts, hand orientation, action, and return remain exact.

alternateAssessments.name: Tempo or Brief Comfortable Endpoint Pause
alternateAssessments.rationale: Controlled pace and a short non-forced pause change exposure rather than identity.

alternateAssessments.name: Repetitions, Sets, or Rest
alternateAssessments.rationale: Volume and recovery change dose rather than the task.

alternateAssessments.name: Stable Knee Cushioning
alternateAssessments.rationale: A stable pad under the knees changes contact comfort without changing the firm palm-support surface or action.

alternateAssessments.name: Wrist Rockers — Palms Up / Flexor Bias
alternateAssessments.rationale: Backs-of-hands support and wrist-flexion bias change the contact surface, joint action, comfort, load, and stop rules.

alternateAssessments.name: Rear-Facing Palms-Down Wrist Rock
alternateAssessments.rationale: Turning the fingers toward the knees changes forearm rotation, wrist line, load direction, and endpoint.

alternateAssessments.name: Side-Facing Wrist Rock
alternateAssessments.rationale: Fingers facing laterally and side-to-side travel change the plane and radial/ulnar loading.

alternateAssessments.name: Quadruped Wrist Circles
alternateAssessments.rationale: Circular center-of-pressure travel adds lateral checkpoints and a direction count.

alternateAssessments.name: Unilateral Wrist Rock
alternateAssessments.rationale: One-hand emphasis changes laterality, load distribution, trunk demand, and failure consequences.

alternateAssessments.name: Finger Pulses / Palm Lifts
alternateAssessments.rationale: Active palm-heel lifting and finger/knuckle pressure are distinct hand actions rather than bodyweight rocking.

alternateAssessments.name: Wrist Lean Isometric / Wrist Support Rock Hold
alternateAssessments.rationale: A sustained isometric endpoint or tall-plank support changes the count, duration, leverage, load, purpose, and fatigue profile.

alternateAssessments.name: Quadruped Wrist Pronation-Supination Shifts
alternateAssessments.rationale: Changing hand orientation during loading adds forearm rotation and multiple directional wrist exposures.

alternateAssessments.name: Raised-Hand Wrist Rock
alternateAssessments.rationale: Wall, counter, bench, or box support changes equipment, support height, load, joint angles, station, and fall consequences.

alternateAssessments.name: Tall-Plank Wrist Rock or Planche Lean
alternateAssessments.rationale: Toe support and longer leverage materially increase wrist, shoulder, trunk, and fatigue demand.

alternateAssessments.name: Banded Wrist Mobilization Rock
alternateAssessments.rationale: An anchored band changes joint force direction, equipment, setup, contraindications, and scope.

alternateAssessments.name: Towel-under-Palm Wrist Rock
alternateAssessments.rationale: Elevating the palm heel changes wrist angle and support interface rather than only knee comfort.

alternateAssessments.name: Fist or Parallette Rock
alternateAssessments.rationale: Neutral-wrist gripping support removes the exact flat-palm wrist-extension interface.

alternateAssessments.name: Loaded or Partner-Resisted Wrist Rock
alternateAssessments.rationale: External load or manual force changes magnitude, consent, equipment, failure risk, and coaching scope.

alternateAssessments.name: Clinical Wrist Range or Pain Assessment
alternateAssessments.rationale: A measured assessment adds examiner protocol, diagnostic/clinical purpose, outcomes, consent, and different stop/escalation rules.
